tagline: Tioga Street, where the mountain gateway keeps its storefronts.
intro: Through Tunkhannock, Business Route 6 takes the name Tioga Street. Lumbering was once carried on extensively here, and the town keeps a historic district of commercial buildings and houses in Queen Anne and Italianate styles, among others. The Dietrich Theatre belongs to that district.
Close by, Tunkhannock Creek finishes its forty-two miles at the Susquehanna. The mountain gateway is also a river town.

moments.title: Tunkhannock Historic District
moments.text: The district runs from the business blocks into the surrounding residential streets, with buildings from 1841 to 1954 in Queen Anne, Italianate and other styles.

moments.title: Tunkhannock Creek
moments.text: At Tunkhannock, the creek joins the Susquehanna after flowing through northeastern Pennsylvania.
